description: Solar UV exposure near the poles is significantly elevated due to ozone depletion — normal SPF habits are insufficient.
response: Crew 16 noted this explicitly before the crater expedition and applied sunscreen to all seven participants.
lesson: Include high-SPF sunscreen in the medical kit and brief the crew. UV risk is easy to underestimate when air temperature is cold — lack of perceived heat masks cumulative dose.
source_citation: SRC-hypatia-iii-brief, Part IV – Incident and emergency register, §4.6 Logistics and safety, lines 785-790. Register Crew tag: 'C16'. Sol: not stated; 'before the crater expedition' placed at a representative mid-mission point. Confidence (B) rationale: daily-narrative entry. Reclassification note (2026-08-26): originally classified Near-Miss; on review, this entry centres on Crew 16 proactively identifying an underestimated risk and applying sunscreen to the whole crew before exposure occurred, which is better described as a demonstrated good practice than a risk narrowly avoided by circumstance — reclassified to Success/Best Practice.
